cases.candidate_question: Is a zero gradient sufficient for a local minimum?
cases.mathematical_reason: Every negative multiple c‖x‖² has gradient zero at the origin, but its value decreases along any nonzero direction. The supplied vector excludes the zero-dimensional exceptional space.

cases.candidate_question: Does a local minimum guarantee that an actual derivative exists and vanishes?
cases.mathematical_reason: The norm has a global minimum at zero and is not differentiable there on any nontrivial real inner-product space. Fermat requires differentiability; totalized gradient zero alone does not provide it.

cases.candidate_question: Does the characterization local minimum iff x=0 hold also for c=0?
cases.mathematical_reason: On a nontrivial space, c=0 makes the objective constant, so every nonzero point is also a minimum. Strict positivity is needed for the unique-location characterization.

cases.candidate_question: Can the nonnegative coefficient assumption be dropped from the claim that zero minimizes c‖x‖²?
cases.mathematical_reason: If c<0 and a nonzero vector exists, every small nonzero multiple has value below the value at zero. The stationary-not-minimum theorem supplies the formal general refutation.

cases.candidate_question: Does an exact solution of Ax=b have to be the unique minimizer of the squared residual?
cases.mathematical_reason: No. For A=0 and b=0 on a nontrivial domain, every point is an exact solution and minimizer. Injectivity or another uniqueness hypothesis would be necessary; the card deliberately asserts neither.
